forRuling: R38 — en-bloc registration of the insert-set keys that block acq-2026-09-14-cardboardconnection-2 (PR #2157)
status: AWAITING DREW. This file is a PROPOSAL and a census. It registers nothing, routes nothing, and no lane reads it.

whatIsBlocked.reason: Each of these products numbers its named insert sets from 1 with its OWN players, so 4193 addresses on the product key are claimed by two or more different cards (2019 Donruss Football #1 is Patrick Mahomes II in `base`, Todd Gurley II in `action-all-pros`, and Peyton Manning in `all-time-gridiron-kings`). Per lib/insert-set-key.cjs the unit of refusal is the FILE, so all 8 stay BLOCKED until these keys are registered.

howToRule: THE KEY IS PROPOSED IN THE QUALIFIED FORM `<parentSetKey>-<subset>`, not bare. Measured on main: 0 of the 122 bare subset names is a registered product key, while 2 of the qualified forms ALREADY are (panini-donruss-rookie-phenom-jersey-autographs, panini-donruss-signature-marks). The qualified form is also the shape the 2026-09-13 insider acquisition already ships under (panini-rookies-and-stars-rookies-signatures).

A BARE KEY WOULD COLLIDE ACROSS SPORTS. `jersey-kings` and `the-rookies` each appear in BOTH basketball and football products, and `retro-series` in five cells across both sports. Those are different cards sharing an insert name, so the parent must stay in the key.

REGISTRATION IS TWO HALVES, BOTH IN src. productSetKeys.ts needs the entry AND normalizeSetKey needs an anchored rule, or the key is not a fixed point and the rows land where nothing can reach them (lib/insert-set-key.cjs records normalizeSetKey('panini-prizm-fifa-world-cup-guardians') -> 'panini-prizm', a fold PAST the product key onto the bare flagship).
NOTHING HERE IS MINTED FROM A SALE. Every subsetCategory below is a section title printed on the cardboardconnection checklist for that product, and `rows` is the number of cards that section lists.

A DOUBLED WORD IS THE SOURCE'S OWN NAME, NOT A BUG. `panini-donruss-donruss-threads` looks wrong and is not: the insert set printed on the checklist is literally "Donruss Threads" inside the Donruss product. The proposal keeps the printed name rather than trimming it, because trimming to `panini-donruss-threads` would invent a name the source does not use. Same shape for any other repeated-brand insert below. Drew may prefer the trimmed spelling — that is part of what this ruling decides.
